task: Prepare the v1 public-launch positioning and the next steps to ship it, using only claims that are true today.
project_summary: A small team is launching a developer tool. Early users bounce off a feature-list homepage; the team needs one sharp promise and an honest launch that doesn't overclaim.
current_direction: Lead the launch with a single promise and prove it with one 30-second example; defer everything not shippable today.

decisions.title: Lead with one promise, not a feature list
decisions.body: The hero states a single outcome the product delivers today; features live below the fold.
decisions.rationale: In user interviews, first-time visitors skimmed feature lists and left without understanding the core value.
decisions.tradeoffs: Some real capabilities won't be front-and-centre at launch; accepted for a clearer first impression.

evidence.claim: First-time visitors understood the product faster when shown one outcome instead of a feature list

sources.label: Positioning: make your product easy to understand (April Dunford)

constraints: Every public claim must be true today — no vaporware or unreleased capabilities.
One promise in the hero, not a feature list.
Do not overstate what the hosted platform does versus the open-source piece.
boundaries: Draft launch copy + the plan only; do not publish the site or post anything.
Use only real, confirmed product capabilities.
what_to_avoid: Claiming roadmap items as if they already ship.
open_questions: Which of the two candidate taglines converts better in a quick test?
Is pricing ready for launch, or should v1 be waitlist-only?
next_steps: Write the hero promise + one 30-second example.
List the true, shippable-today capabilities for the section below the fold.
Decide waitlist vs. open signup based on pricing readiness.
definition_of_done: A launch page whose hero is a single true promise backed by one concrete example, with no claim that isn't shippable today, and a clear go/no-go on waitlist vs. open signup.

recommended_assistant.reason: This is positioning and launch-copy drafting under hard truthfulness constraints.
